sentences.text: 3. A perusal of Annexure F order shows that the prayer for further investigation was rejected in view of the settled legal position that such a prayer at the instance of the de facto complainant cannot be entertained after framing of charge and commencement of trial.
4. I heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.
5. The Apex court in Amrutbhai Shambhubhai Patel v. Sumanbhai Kantibhai Patel and Ors.

entities.text: Amrutbhai Shambhubhai Patel v. Sumanbhai Kantibhai Patel and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
[(2017)
SCC OnLine SC 86]

, while holding that further investigation cannot be ordered at the instance of the de facto complainant, after the charge is framed, also made it clear that the prohibition will not apply if such a request is made by the Investigating Officer.

Being contextually relevant, paragraph 49 of the judgment is extracted hereunder;
"49.

On an overall survey of the pronouncements of this Court on the scope and purport of Section 173(8) of the Code and the consistent trend of explication thereof,
we are thus disposed to hold that though the investigating agency concerned has been invested with the power to undertake further investigation desirably after informing the court 2025:KER:52284 CRL.MC NO. 5876 OF 2025 thereof, before which it had submitted its report and obtaining its approval, no such power is available therefor to the learned Magistrate after cognizance has been taken on the basis of the earlier report, process has been issued and the accused has entered appearance in response thereto.
At that stage, neither the learned Magistrate suo motu nor on an application filed by the complainant/informant can direct further investigation.

Such a course would be open only on the request of the investigating agency and that too, in circumstances warranting further investigation on the detection of material evidence only to secure fair investigation and trial, the life purpose of the adjudication in hand."
6.
The courts below were therefore fully justified in dismissing the application seeking further investigation filed by the petitioner.
Needless to say, if the investigating officer deems it appropriate to file an application for further investigation, the court below is bound to pass appropriate orders.
The Crl.M.C. is closed accordingly.
